title: Integration playbook + pilot onboarding — Arcturus Systems
summary: Discovery / scoping call to align success criteria, workload sizing, and benchmark plan for a 6-week pilot. Primary focus: OpenAI-compatible endpoints + SDK integration, function/tool calling for downstream services, structured JSON output, and performance/cost targets. Agreed to run a 72-hour benchmark with Redwood hosted and a Dedicated config. Security and SSO questions noted; Redwood to share SOC2 and VPC docs.

Security (SSO, KMS, audit logs) and deployment options

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-10-19
Start: 16:30 UTC
Duration: ~62 min
Attendees: Sofia Lin (Redwood AE), Marcus Hale (Redwood SE), Priya Desai (Redwood SA briefly), Daniel Cho (Arcturus CTO), Maya Reyes (Lead ML Eng), Hector Alvarez (SRE), Lina Park (PM)

Auto-Summary:
- Arcturus wants to run a 6-week pilot to validate integration with their product search and incident summarization pipelines.
- Key must-haves: OpenAI-style API compatibility for minimal code changes, reliable function/tool calling for internal DB calls, structured JSON output schema validated at the edge, and predictable 95th/99th percentile latencies under load.

[00:00] Sofia (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros — I'll hand to Marcus for the technical run-down and then we can go through your use cases.
[00:23] Marcus (SE): Yeah hi, Marcus here. At a high level we'll want to map your current endpoints and the SDK calls you make today to Redwood's OpenAI-compatible endpoints. That should let you reuse client code with minimal change.
[00:45] Daniel (CTO): Great. The main constraint for us is we have a production search pipeline where the LLM is in the critical path for query rewriting and rerank hints. If latency spikes over 200ms p95 we start to see timeouts upstream.
[01:10] Maya (ML): And we plan on sampling ~1.2M requests/month initially, avg prompt tokens ~350, but some workflows are Chat-style where context grows to 2k tokens.
[01:34] Hector (SRE): Also network: we have strict egress windows and require peered VPC for the dedicated pilot. Full audit logs are required for the pilot.
[02:02] Marcus: Ok noted. For the search path, suggest focusing benchmarks on 1) 95/99 latency for 512 and 2k seq lengths, 2) tail latency during autoscaling events, 3) cost per 1M tokens with quantized variants.
[02:30] Lina (PM): On success criteria, we want to measure both latency and output quality — e.g., rewrite accuracy measured against our human-eval set and throughput to support 100 RPS sustained with 500 RPS bursts.
[02:58] Sofia: A couple quick clarifications: when you say function/tool calling, do you mean you want Redwood to call your internal microservices via HTTP edges, or you want the SDK to emit structured function calls that your backend will execute?
[03:17] Maya: Ideally both. For some features we want the model to return a JSON payload specifying the DB query and parameters (structured output). For others we want Redwood to call a registered tool (e.g., our inventory service) to fetch live data and stream results back.
[03:42] Marcus: That maps to two modes: 1) function-calling where the model returns a typed JSON schema that you validate and then your app runs, and 2) server-side tool integration where Redwood can be configured to call your tool endpoints under a secure auth flow. We support both in the hosted and Dedicated plane.
[04:10] Daniel: Security-wise, server-side tooling sounds heavy — we'd prefer the SDK-first pattern for now, because we keep all secrets in our VPC. But for latency-sensitive calls, having Redwood call close-by tools might save 50-80ms.
[04:33] Marcus: Right, that's the tradeoff — latency vs control. For the pilot we can do SDK-first + optional proxy tooling for selected endpoints.
[04:50] Priya (Redwood SA): Quick note on structured output: we recommend shipping a strict JSON Schema for the model to emit, then run schema validation at the edge. That reduces downstream parsing errors and lowers false positive rates.
[05:10] Maya: Good. We'll share our current schema for rewrites and incident summaries.
[05:25] Hector: On telemetry — we need token-level tracing and per-request IDs so we can correlate with our logs. Can Redwood attach trace ids and expose token timing?
[05:40] Marcus: Yes, token-level timing and request_id passthrough are available. We'll also surface p50/p95/p99 and token-cost in the Console.
[05:56] Lina: For the pilot benchmark, what's the recommended workload shape?
[06:05] Marcus: We typically recommend a three-phase: cold-start ramp (simulate 0 -> 100 RPS over 15 minutes), sustained load (72 hours at target RPS and a 1% spike every 10 minutes), and stress spikes (burst tests to 5x sustained). We'll include both 512 and 2k token profiles.
[06:30] Daniel: Do you run the benchmark on Redwood hosted, or can we trial Dedicated? We want to compare both.
[06:40] Sofia: We can run a comparative benchmark: Hosted first to validate feature parity and quality, followed by a Dedicated reservation (3-4 GPU nodes) to measure tail latency and cost. We'll include quantized runs (fp16, int8) where applicable.
[06:58] Maya: What's your expected latency on Dedicated for 2k context under 100 RPS?
[07:05] Marcus: Ballpark: for Llama-2-style LLMs optimized with KV-cache and continuous batching, p95 for 2k could be 120–220ms depending on model and quantization. We will give you precise numbers from the pilot runs.
[07:30] Hector: We also need to ensure deterministic rollouts — if you auto-fallback to a smaller model under load, we want a flag so our QA can detect it.
[07:44] Priya: We surface model-variant in headers; rollouts are controlled via route policies in Console and you can pin a model per route. We'll add the QA flag to the pilot config.
[08:02] Sofia: Let's talk success criteria concretely — Lina, can you confirm the pass/fail items?
[08:12] Lina: Sure. Passed pilot if: 1) p95 latency <= 180ms for 512 tokens and <= 300ms for 2k tokens on Dedicated; 2) model quality hit >= 92% on your rewrite test set (we'll accept +/-1.5%); 3) cost per 1M tokens under $X (TBD but target is 40% lower than current vendor); 4) security checklist items met (SOC2 docs, VPC peering, audit logs).
[08:46] Sophie: (laughs) Sofia: I like the concrete targets. We'll draft the SLO doc and include baseline numbers.
[08:55] Maya: About SDKs — we have an existing OpenAI-compatible wrapper in Python and Node. We want minimal changes — ideally we just swap endpoint and API key.
[09:12] Marcus: That's supported. Redwood's OpenAI-compatible endpoints accept the same request shapes, including function-style JSON in the messages and structured output hints. We do have slight differences in streaming and tool registration APIs — we'll document those.
[09:33] Daniel: Can we keep the same client-side retry semantics? We have exponential backoff configured at the SDK.
[09:41] Marcus: Yes, you can keep your retries. We'll also provide an SDK plug-in that surfaces token-cost and per-call metadata.
[09:52] Lina: A question on tool calling auth — if Redwood calls our internal inventory service, how is auth handled?
[10:01] Priya: We support mutual-TLS for Dedicated/VPC peering and signed temporary credentials for hosted integrations. For the pilot, given Arcturus' requirement, we'll propose VPC peering and mutual-TLS for a small set of tool endpoints.
[10:20] Hector: That sounds reasonable — we'll likely only allow two endpoints at first (inventory, pricing).
[10:28] Maya: For structured responses, we want the model to output an array of objects: [{action: 'rewrite', score: 0.95, rewrite_text: '...'}]. Can Redwood validate and reject malformed payloads before they hit prod?
[10:42] Marcus: Yes, the validation layer can drop or flag responses that don't match your JSON Schema. There's also an option to return a parse_error hint to the client.
[10:53] Sofia: Ok, timeline — we propose: 1) Gather workload & schema (this week), 2) Redwood shares SOW & bench harness (by Fri), 3) Bench run next week (72h), 4) Pilot onboarding and QA week after. That fits a 6-week pilot end-to-end.
[11:12] Daniel: Works for us.
[11:20] Lina: A few edge questions — how do you handle model upgrades during pilot?
[11:26] Priya: We can pin a model and do canary rollouts per route. Any upgrade will be a controlled canary with automatic fallback to the pinned version if quality deviates beyond thresholds you set.
[11:40] Hector: For logs retention, what's included in the standard Package? We need 12 months for audit.
[11:47] Marcus: Enterprise add-on for extended retention — we'll include retention options in the SOW.
[11:55] Maya: One more: for cost measurement, can you provide token-level cost broken down by model variant for the benchmark?
[12:04] Marcus: Yes, we'll output a CSV with per-request token counts, model variant, and cost estimate.
[12:12] Sofia: Great. Let's do a quick recap and owners.
[12:18] Sofia: Items: Arcturus to send workload traces and schemas (Maya). Redwood to send SOW, benchmark harness and SOC2/KMS docs (Sofia, Marcus). Schedule kickoff for week of 10/25.
[12:35] Daniel: Thanks, that's helpful.
[12:40] Sofia: Any other blockers?
[12:43] Hector: Need to confirm firewall windows with security team—I'll ping you.
[12:47] Lina: No blockers otherwise.
[12:49] Sofia: Perfect. We'll follow up in email and create the pilot workspace with initial credentials. Thanks everyone.

Questions (raised):

End of meeting.
